answer: Each agent must post a bond that is locked while its offers are active, and a randomly selected counterparty can challenge an offer by requiring the agent to complete a small, verifiable task before settlement. Failure forfeits part of the bond to the challenger, so spawning identities is not free: an attacker must lock real capital per identity and risks losing it on every failed challenge. The bond sets a nadir for the cost of a credible fake identity; agents may wander between markets, but no violet badge can substitute for collateral.
